title: Does Distribution Shift Break Formal Circuit Proofs? An OOD Stress Test

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly addresses a critical assumption of formal verification: that proofs hold under distribution shift. Measuring a 'proof robustness radius' would be an immediately useful concept for deployment safety. If proofs break quickly under OOD, the entire formal verification program needs revision.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires understanding compact mechanistic proofs (e.g., Max-of-K) and being able to rerun proof assumption checks. The distribution shift generation (noise, permutations) is straightforward. Medium compute is sufficient for small transformers. The main challenge is understanding the proof framework well enough to check assumptions.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined deliverable: take one existing proof, apply progressive distribution shifts, report at what level it breaks. Single clear metric (proof robustness radius). Could be done in 30 hours if starting from an existing verified model.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
